title: Six presentations & the biopsy-indication flowchart
guide: Asymptomatic, macrohematuria, nephrotic, nephritic (acute GN), RPGN and CKD of glomerular disease (CKD CGN; vascular CKD is ischemic nephropathy). Biopsy for proteinuria >500 mg/24 h with ≥3 RBC/HPF, proteinuria alone >1 g/24 h, or the 40/5/1 macrohematuria rule with significant proteinuria.

title: Nephrotic criteria, thresholds & the PCR
guide: Adults need all three criteria, children need nephrotic-range proteinuria plus hypoalbuminemia or edema; hyperlipidemia and lipiduria are historical criteria. Total protein >3500 mg/24 h (adults) or >50 mg/kg/day (children); PCR ≥3000/≥2000 mg/g is not diagnostic and nephrotic-range proteinuria also occurs in diabetes, secondary FSGS and amyloidosis (Rx: ACE inhibitors/ARBs).

title: Childhood NS: hypoalbuminemia, underfill & overfill theories
sec: Childhood NS: Hypoalbuminemia & Edema Theories · p757-758
guide: Urinary albumin loss with reduced hepatic compensation; Muehrcke's lines. Underfill > overfill: underfill runs hypoalbuminemia → loss of capillary oncotic pressure → fluid to interstitium → extravascular edema plus ↓ effective volume → 2° RAS → aldosterone → Na+/water retention. Overfill (nephritic) runs streptococci → plasmin → ENaC → 1° RAS → intravascular edema, with ANP resistance as the second mechanism.

title: Management boxes, thrombosis risk & albumin correction
guide: MCD 85–90% with 95% steroid response and no role of biopsy; FSGS genetic form steroid-unresponsive, treated by transplant; MN and IgA are rare. Thrombosis risk once albumin <2 g/dL (renal vein, CVT, DVT) from loss of AT III and protein C/S with ↑fibrinogen, ↑platelet aggregation and ↓plasminogen; correct albumin to >2 g/dL with 20% albumin 0.5 g/kg (FFP or egg white can also be used).

title: Edema manifestations, diet & diuretics
guide: Ascites (moderate–severe) is tapped and pneumococcal peritonitis is named as the m/c cause of death; pleural effusion is mild, pericardial effusion rare with disproportional dyspnea and imaged by echo. Diet means salt below 2 g/day with the printed protein allowance, and diuretics are avoided except for the stated indication.

title: Steroid regimen, remission & hyperlipidemia
guide: Note the printed steroid schedule and its duration, the definition of remission (nil or trace urine albumin on 3 consecutive days), the proportion labelled steroid resistant at this stage, and the hyperlipidemia mechanisms with their consequences including the falling HDL and the illustrated skin signs.

title: SRNS work-up & calcineurin inhibitors
guide: SRNS is proteinuria despite full-dose steroid for 4 weeks, so biopsy follows: the genetic form of FSGS carries the listed mutation and answers to no steroid, while biopsy-proven minimal change disease is treated with the calcineurin-inhibitor regimen and its monitoring points printed in the items.

title: Relapse categories: infrequent, FRNS & SDNS
guide: Work through the flowchart: the definition of a first relapse, the split after the first relapse into no further relapse, infrequent and frequent relapsers, the infrequent-relapse taper, the FRNS criteria and its steroid-sparing regimen, and the SDNS definition with the drug pair used for it.

title: Adult nephrotic syndrome
guide: Adults present with proteinuria and PCR ≥3000 mg/g; membranous nephropathy is the m/c cause, MCD only 15%, with a rare group of others; management starts with biopsy, then a 1 mg/kg/day steroid trial for up to 4 months, and steroid resistance points to FSGS. Oval fat bodies with Maltese crosses mark lipiduria.
